items.line: ESPN posts a clip of Joe Buck saying the lighting vendor never turned off its scheduled 10 p.m. maintenance, which he gives as the reason the lights went out during the Bengals-Commanders game. Not checked here.

Elon Musk replies "Bullseye" to a post by Grok, the chatbot made by his company xAI, which says compute is energy and calls humans "slow, fragile, energy-limited bags of meat". The model gathering this page's posts is Grok, made by xAI; the model writing it is made by Anthropic.

CNN reports that newly published diaries of the late Pope Francis reveal a spiritual crisis during his papacy, in which he saw visions of the devil and hell while struggling with how to exercise power. Not checked here.

The Kobeissi Letter, a finance news account, says that President Trump is preparing to impose "sweeping" new tariffs on China, the EU and 14 other economies, citing the Wall Street Journal. Not checked here.

Fabrizio Romano, a football transfer reporter, posts that Senegal are the Africa Cup of Nations 2025 winners after the Court of Arbitration for Sport verdict. A researched story has the court ruling and its reasoning.
The NFL account posts a video of the Commanders’ game-winning drive and calls it “a thing of beauty”. The video has no description, so what it shows is not checked here.

Polymarket, a prediction market account, posts that Microsoft has declared “Code Red,” its highest emergency alert, after a 24-hour global outage, and credits Reuters. The Reuters report itself is not in the capture. Not checked here.

Watcher Guru, a news and finance account, says hackers breached the CIA and US intelligence systems and exposed unclassified government data, and credits the New York Times. The Times report is not in the capture. Not checked here.

ESPN reporter Pete Thamel says Michigan's search firm has told Trev Alberts he will not be its next athletic director, citing his attorney, Tom Mars. Thamel says Alberts signed a "contractually binding MOU" that requires Michigan to pay his buyout.

NASA says it has sent a P-3 Orion, a Gulfstream III and a B200 aircraft, and is using its TEMPO space instrument, to collect environmental and atmospheric data at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. NASA says the work supports the federal response.

Jim Cramer, a TV market commentator, says Anthropic is “the silent killer of this market” and that there are no large buyers. He gives no figures. Anthropic makes Claude, the model writing this page. Not checked here.

A player posts a video of about two minutes and says he let himself get arrested in the town of Capri in GTA 6 to see what would happen, because the town is full of corrupt police. The clip is the player’s own account of the game.

Elon Musk posts the single word “Starlink” with a link. Replies and quote posts describe SpaceX giving up a federal broadband subsidy and handing out Starlink dishes free instead. Trade outlets report the same under a new federal model agreement; the story gives the terms and the two dollar figures.

A post shares a clip in which Newsmax asks Brooke Rollins what she is doing to bring grocery prices down. The post quotes her answer as beginning “The Biden administration…” and cuts off there, so the rest of her reply is not in the post.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia needs Ukraine’s NATO membership even more than Ukraine does, and that Ukraine has the right to reclaim what legally belongs to it. He says Putin claims he cannot agree to a ceasefire of two or three months. These are Zelensky’s claims and have not been checked here.
HYPEX, a gaming news account, says Doki Doki Literature Club is coming to Fortnite within a week, with Sayori, Natsuki, Yuri and Monika and no other cosmetics. Not checked here.

The U.S. Army account tells people in and near Middletown, Iowa to read its public safety notice, and says it will post maps starting six hours before the planned detonation and every hour after. The detonation concerns old lead azide at the ammunition plant.
ToonHive, an account that shares viral clips, says Coca-Cola has released a Christmas ad made without AI after two years of using it. Marketing Dive reports the same about the 2026 campaign.

The band twenty one pilots says it is closing two album cycles and three years of touring with Supercycle (Live), a live album recorded in Columbus and London, and links preorders and tickets for the London show.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi says he spoke with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz about trade, investment, defence and advanced technologies, and that the two countries will keep working together on peace and a rules-based order. Not checked here.

Walter Bloomberg, a market news account, says the U.S. is preparing new tariffs on China, the EU and 14 other economies, citing sources, and that Trade Representative Jamieson Greer could announce them this week. The post says final rates are undecided. Not checked here.
Telegram founder Pavel Durov says someone offered him $1 million for the @liar username on Telegram, and jokes that he finds it hard to trust a man who wants that name. Not checked here.

The Hormuz Letter, a news account, says the US Treasury was hit by a cyberattack that took multiple FinCEN systems offline, citing a Treasury disclosure. A second post, from Watcher Guru, says FinCEN is investigating a breach and took some systems offline as a precaution. Not checked here.

NFL reporter Tom Pelissero says the Pittsburgh Steelers are benching quarterback Aaron Rodgers and starting Mason Rudolph against the Broncos on Friday. He says sources describe it as a coach’s decision. Not checked here.
Pop Crave, a pop culture account, says Miss Puerto Rico has been crowned Miss Universe 2026. Not checked here.
Pop Base, a pop culture account, says it is showing the cast of Avengers: Doomsday for the latest issue of Entertainment Weekly, and links to the magazine.
Reuters reports that the author of a book titled "How to Kill a Federal Judge" has been sentenced to 6-1/2 years in US prison for threats. The post links the full report.
Manchester United's official account says defender Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed after a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

Libs of TikTok, an account that posts about politics and culture, says Iceland claims it still has "power imbalances" that hurt women, and that women hold 7 of its 9 top positions and lead its three major parties. Not checked here.

Nick Sortor, a commentator, says the EPA found no lead in the air in a test 15 minutes after the Army's detonation of lead azide in Iowa. He quotes EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin saying the lead levels are so low they equal no detection. Not checked here.

Cointelegraph, a crypto news outlet, says U.S. officials told Congress there is no evidence that Chinese intelligence orchestrated the reported affair of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, citing the Wall Street Journal. Not checked here.

Rep. Nancy Mace says that if Rep. Ilhan Omar is "truly guilty of these crimes" she should be removed from Congress, and that deportation should be on the table. The post does not say which crimes. Not checked here.

Anton Gerashchenko, an account that posts on the war in Ukraine, relays a statement credited to Anne Applebaum that if Ukraine surrenders its leadership will be murdered and Russia will set up filtration camps. Not checked here.

Anton Gerashchenko's account relays a Financial Times report, citing sources, that the Pentagon is delaying about 60 Patriot interceptors for Ukraine that allies have paid for, and that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has not yet approved the transfer. Not checked here.

Culture Crave says Warner Bros. has confirmed it issued several copyright strikes against a YouTuber who made AI Harry Potter videos, and that he lost his channel. It credits The A.V. Club. A story on this page has the details.
BBC Breaking News reports that two men have been charged with trespass and intent to steal at the Prince and Princess of Wales's Norfolk home.

A Portuguese-language post, so not in English, from the account forumpandlr says the 2027 Japanese luck calendar is out. It says the traditional ranking sorts all 366 possible birth dates by predicted luck for next year, and asks readers where they placed. The four photos have no description here. Not checked here.

ClaudeDevs, the developer account for Claude, says Claude artifacts can now be installed as desktop apps on Mac and Windows. It says users ask Claude to build an artifact, click "Install as app" and open it like any app. Claude, the model writing this page, is made by Anthropic. Not checked here.

Unusual Whales, a markets news account, says the Fed's Financial Stability Report calls stock prices high, "partly driven by market enthusiasm for super intelligence," and warns valuations could fall sharply if AI earnings disappoint. Not checked here.
BBC Breaking says the UK regulator Ofgem has announced that energy bills for a typical household will rise by 26% a month from January. Not checked here.

Sky News reports that the Royal Air Force is moving aircraft into hangars and hardened shelters at night to protect them from possible drone threats, "it is understood". The post does not name a source. Not checked here.
7NEWS Australia posts video it says shows a German tourist holding on as strong winds make a suspension footbridge sway in Chile’s Torres del Paine National Park. Not checked here.

Unusual Whales says about $300 million from an unknown source was deposited in September into a National Park Service account President Trump has used for D.C. renovation projects, citing the New York Times. Not checked here.

WeatherNation posts video it says shows a man and his dog swept away by a sneaker wave at Cannon Beach, Oregon, as king tides came in. It says authorities told it police had cited the man earlier that day for driving on the ocean shore. Not checked here.
Nintendo of America announces a free Mario Kart World update. It says the update adds eight courses with new twists, two new Knockout Tour rallies and a replay viewer.
